subject: Post-call: performance targets & reproducible benchmark plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@payflux.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: performance targets & reproducible benchmark plan

Thanks again for taking the time earlier, Elena — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on a reproducible benchmark run.

Recap (from call)
- Primary objective: validate that our hosted/dedicated deployment can meet PayFlux latency SLOs under representative traffic.
- Target SLOs you called out: p95 end-to-end response latency <= 150ms for streaming use-cases (up to ~512 token responses), sustained throughput ~200 req/s, concurrency ~40, with bursts to 500 req/s for up to 5 minutes.
- Streaming semantics: client expects token-level flushes as candidates are generated (not full-response only).
- Success criteria: Meet SLOs for 95% of requests for three independent 30-minute windows and produce reproducible reports (raw traces + aggregated metrics).

What we need from PayFlux to move to a deterministic benchmark
1) Representative prompt set (jsonl) or a link to S3 — ideally 500–1,000 prompts with distribution of short/long contexts. I attached an initial sample (initial_prompt_sample.jsonl) to show the expected format.
2) Traffic shape: target QPS timeline (sustained + burst windows) and concurrency profile.
3) Any special tokens/stop sequences or deterministic seeds you require.
4) Confirmation on security constraints (VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, or if we should route through Dedicated).

Our proposed methodology (high level)
- Warm-up period: 5 minutes at 20% target QPS to populate KV cache.
- Measurement windows: run three independent 30-minute passes separated by 10-minute cool-downs.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (request receive -> final token emitted), token emission latency for streaming (time to first token, per-token spacing), throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, and 95th-percentile tail on memory pressure.
- Reproducibility: we'll provide the exact harness (Docker + runbook) and a canonical set of flags to reproduce locally and in your environment.

Next steps / proposed timeline
- You share the prompt set + traffic profile by EOD Friday (2026-03-06).
- We provision a dedicated benchmark window next week (suggest Tue 2026-03-10 10:00–14:00 PT).
- Nikhil will follow up with the harness and measurement definitions.

Attachments: initial_prompt_sample.jsonl (format example)

Thanks — I can hop on a quick follow if any of this needs clarifying.

Best,

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our end and answering a few items: 

Confirmed targets
- p95 <= 150ms (end-to-end) for responses up to ~512 tokens when streamed.
- Sustained throughput 200 req/s, concurrency 40. Burst to 500 req/s tolerated for up to 5 minutes.

Notes / clarifications
- For streaming we need token-level flushes every ~50ms if possible; primary UX requirement is low time-to-first-byte.
- We will provide a prompt set (~800 prompts) with tags for short/medium/long branches. Link: s3://payflux-bench/prompts/reprompt-set-v2.jsonl. Team will also drop a small subset that must be treated as high-priority (real-money flows).
- Security: we prefer Dedicated within our VPC for the benchmark if Redwood can support the interface; otherwise, an allowlist of IP ranges works.

Actionables from PayFlux
- I’ll share the prompt set and a short traffic spec doc (QPS shapes + ETA for bursts) by 2026-03-05 COB.
- Our infra lead (cc’d) will coordinate the connectivity requirements.

Thanks — looking forward to the harness and runbook. If the proposed Tue slot works, we’ll lock it in.

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>

Elena / Camila — quick technical addendum with an explicit methodology and measurement definitions so the results are reproducible and comparable across environments. I attached a short readme (redwood_benchmark_readme.md) that mirrors the repo.

Measurement definitions (precise)
- Request latency (end-to-end): measured from the moment the client TCP connection sends the first request byte (or HTTP request start) until the last token is emitted and the response stream is closed. For streaming, we also capture time-to-first-token (TTFT) and per-token inter-arrival distributions.
- Token emission latency: measured per-token using server-side monotonic timestamps; aggregated per-response to compute mean and p95 token spacing.
- Throughput: successful completed responses per second (excluding retried/failed attempts).
- Error accounting: categorize 4xx/5xx vs transient timeouts; report both absolute counts and rates per measurement window.

Benchmark harness & reproducibility
- Harness: containerized runner that drives clients with a configurable traffic profile file. The runner includes a deterministic RNG seed, request pacing options, and optional synthetic jitter to simulate network conditions.
- Warm-up: 5 minutes at 20% nominal QPS.
- Cache policy: we will run with KV cache enabled to reflect production (but will also run a control iteration with cache disabled if you want to measure cold-start semantics).
- Hardware config: we will document instance types (GPU model, mem), kernel versions, and quantization/precision flags. All runs will include raw CPU/GPU telemetry and per-request traces.
- Reproducibility artifacts: harness config, exact prompt file version (SHA), captured trace logs, and an aggregated report generator (CSV + JSON + human-readable summary).

Streaming specifics
- We'll report: TTFT (ms), median inter-token gap, per-response last-token latency. For the SLO we’ll enforce p95 of end-to-end response latency and call out token-level tail behaviors separately.
- If PayFlux needs different chunking behavior (e.g., flush every N tokens vs time-based flush), include that in the traffic profile.

Request: please confirm the prompt file URI and whether the high-priority subset must be run at a higher sampling rate during the benchmark. Also confirm if you require the Dedicated deployment for security.

If the Tue 2026-03-10 window works, we will: provision infra, share the harness repo (immutable tag), and a short runbook with exact curl/wss commands to reproduce.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
